answer_1.quote: This paper focuses on lexical selection, a key aspect of translation that requires using context in a source sentence to determine the best translation for an ambiguous source word from several target-language options.
answer_1.outputs: Lexical selection in translation, rule generation for concept variations

answer_2.quote: Accuracy is measured as the proportion of sentences for which the model selects the correct lexical variation.

answer_4.quote: We work with bilingual speakers to ensure our methods and data faithfully represent the processes associated with translation under concept variation. For each language, we recruit from Prolific three annotators who are fluent English speakers and native speakers of the target language.
answer_4.guideline: All three expert annotators for each language provide feedback on the extracted variations, including whether each variation matches the meaning of the English lexeme (for computing precision) and whether any key variations are missing from the set (for computing recall).
criteria: matches the meaning of the English lexeme
